title: Fast Graph Laplacian Estimation using Effective Resistance
summary: The method replaces iterative sparsity-regularized maximum-likelihood estimation of graph Laplacians for Gaussian Markov random fields with a non-iterative estimator that uses effective resistance as a regularizer followed by sparsification. The cost is reduced edge and weight recovery accuracy relative to iterative approaches; compute requirements are low and fit constrained infrastructure easily. It can fail in the underdetermined regime (fewer samples than nodes) or when the Gaussian Markov random field assumption does not hold, producing inaccurate topology estimates.
rationale: This is a graph signal processing method for inferring network topology from node observations, which falls outside the LLM inference, training, and agent workflows that define the reader's production practice.
technique: Non-iterative Laplacian estimation via effective resistance

claims.statement: The method replaces iterative sparsity-regularized maximum-likelihood estimation of graph Laplacians for Gaussian Markov random fields with a non-iterative estimator that uses effective resistance as a regularizer followed by sparsification. The cost is reduced edge and weight recovery accuracy relative to iterative approaches; compute requirements are low and fit constrained infrastructure easily. It can fail in the underdetermined regime (fewer samples than nodes) or when the Gaussian Markov random field assumption does not hold, producing inaccurate topology estimates.
Computational cost for moderately sized graphs can be substantially reduced, with some trade-off in edge and weight recovery; no numeric factor is reported in the abstract.
